title: Continuous depth-time Givens views versus shared and embedded vector fields
hypothesis: For a stable 2D vector field rotating smoothly with depth time, a continuous Givens Mirror view trained on t in [0,1] achieves extrapolated t=2 endpoint NRMSE <=1.1x a simple linear time-embedding field while using <=90% its actual bytes and the same solver NFE.
mirror_coordinate: continuous depth-time angle omega*t applied as Q(t) A Q(t)^T
logical_multiplicity: a continuum of depth-specific vector-field roles from one shared field
controls: four discrete depth-bin matrices with last-bin extrapolation

task.teacher: A(t)=Q(omega*t) A0 Q(omega*t)^T with omega=0.7 and stable eigenvalues

development.selection_metric: lowest validation derivative NRMSE for t<=1

success_gate: On each fresh world, Mirror t=2 endpoint NRMSE <=1.1x linear time embedding, Mirror bytes <=90% linear embedding bytes, and identical RK4 NFE.
failure_gate: Mirror misses extrapolation quality or byte threshold, or simple time embedding dominates at comparable bytes.
boundaries: Teacher matches the continuous rotation view family; aligned feasibility only.
One low-dimensional linear system; no Transformer depth or language model claim.
Fixed-step RK4; adaptive solver stability untested.
